correctness.rationale: Example 4.1 gives the fixed plane curve, distinct from the ambient K3. On taking a coordinate-sign quotient, squaring the flipped coordinate gives a quadratic; its discriminant is 32(t⁴+3t²+1) for x₀ and 32(t⁴−3t²+1) for each of x₁,x₂. These give smooth genus-one models after rescaling over ℂ (the two distinct nonzero roots for t² yield four distinct roots), and t→it identifies the two forms. Substitution u=(w+1)/t² gives (u²−1)t²=2u+a, so X=2u and Y=2t(u²−1) yield the stated cubic with roots −2,2,−a. The Legendre parameter is (2−a)/4=−1/4 or 5/4, giving j=148176/25 by the Legendre formula. Exact independent checks: python3 -B /workspace/audit-evidence/4_legendre_check.py, output in 4_replay.txt in that directory. Squaring all coordinates gives the full sign-group quotient (generic fibers are the sign orbits); its conic determinant is −80. The invariant holomorphic forms for each involution thus have dimension one and no common trivial character, so they are the three different nontrivial Klein-four characters. By conjugation over ℂ the same holds for H¹(O), the tangent space of Pic⁰, so the sum of pullbacks on the Jacobians is an isogeny onto Jac(C). No product polarization or isomorphism of underlying abelian varieties follows.

evidence: Take three identical HLP inputs y²=x(x²+Ax+1), A=6/√5, Δ_i=A²−4=16/5, and P_i chosen so d_i=−4/√5, giving R=−64/(5√5). Their twisting factor is T=−32√5≠0. Proposition 15 gives all mixed coefficients (−A²+AR/Δ_i)/2=−6 and an isogeny from those identical factors over ℂ.

The closest Resultary hits treat flexes of the same pencil, coincidences of two factors for a hyperelliptic family, or characteristic-three Ciani rank distributions. None is a replacement for the directly covering HLP proposition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: HLP with these permitted inputs yields the exact transformed curve and even gives extra isogeny structure; the comparison is stronger than noting that Ciani quartics tend to split.

evidence: Multiplying x₀ by i changes both positive mixed coefficients to −6 without changing fourth powers; the signs commute with this change. This is the symmetric Ciani pencil member C_(−6).

HLP p. 25 gives the invariant-field model v²=(d²−4B₁B₂)y⁴+(2de−4B₁f)y²+(e²−4B₁B₃). With original mixed coefficients (6,6,−6) or cyclic permutation and all B_i=1, this is exactly 32 times the frozen ±3 quartics.

originality.rationale: Howe–Leprévost–Poonen Proposition 15 and its proof already give the plane Ciani-quartic construction, the coordinate-sign quotient formula and the product pullback isogeny (indeed its degree and polarized kernel description). After the diagonal change x₀=iX, x₁=Y, x₂=Z, Example 4.1 is exactly a single specialization with symmetric mixed coefficients −6. The required parameters and j follow by direct substitution, not by a new theorem about a special locus.
residual_risks: The exact catalogue aliases of the pencil member were not exhaustively resolved; no inequivalence with other named models is asserted. The demonstrated HLP coverage does not depend on that issue.
The checked passage of the initiating paper is not a claim about what is absent in every section of that paper.

value.rationale: The fixed curve and its Jacobian are natural objects, but the three models and common j are direct evaluations of existing Ciani quotient formulas and the cube isogeny follows already from the explicit prior construction. Reporting the arithmetic evaluation for the K3 example is useful exposition, not a surviving unknown exact invariant under the audit standard. There is no substantiated distinct claim to repair.
